title: Customer Roadmap Brokerage and Alpha Access Policy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and pilot a disciplined ‘Roadmap Brokerage’ process: a customer-driven intake + negotiation lifecycle for top accounts and escalations that preserves fairness, minimizes unblock time, and protects engineering runway. This ticket covers the intake form, scoring logic, negotiation SLA, and the policy for offering alpha access or paid priority in exchange for scope commitments. Goal: run a 6-week pilot with 4 strategic accounts and measure delivery predictability and revenue impact.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form template live in Confluence and connected to central backlog tracker
Scoring rubric documented and reproducible (same inputs -> same score)
Negotiation SLA defined: response timeline, option matrix (defer, prioritize, commercialize)
Alpha access policy created with legal template for NDAs and success criteria
Pilot runbook for 4 accounts with kickoff, weekly cadence, and decision gates
Dashboards created: open requests, committed scope, expected delivery windows, delta to baseline roadmap
scoring_model: ARR impact: projected ARR delta from feature (0-100)
SLA urgency: external contractual risk or launch date buckets (0-50)
Platform leverage: number of additional customers likely to benefit (0-30)
Implementation complexity: engineering days estimate (negative weight)
Champion strength: customer advocacy and cross-team sponsor (0-20)
Score normalization: map to bands [Defer, Watchlist, Prioritize, Executive Review]
process_flow: 1) Customer intake submitted via account manager form (Confluence -> GH issue template)
2) Triage by PM team within 3 business days to validate ask and completeness
3) Auto-score using scoring_model and surface initial band
4) Commercial conversation: offer options (priority in next cycle, alpha access, paid roadmap slot)
5) If alpha access accepted -> legal/NDAs & success metrics defined; engineering flags feature as alpha in backlog
6) Decision gate: Commit / Defer / Commercialize with documented timelines and fallbacks
7) Post-delivery: run NPS and quality evaluation; log learnings to account dossier
stakeholders: Product Management: Asha Patel (lead), Marcus Liu (owner)
Engineering: Runtime team lead (on-call for feasibility)
metrics: % of prioritized requests delivered within committed window (target >= 80%)
Alpha success rate: % of alpha features meeting success criteria
Developer impact: % increase in scope churn relative to baseline roadmap
Customer satisfaction (post-delivery NPS for pilot accounts)
timeline: Week 0: Finalize intake template, scoring rubric, legal alpha clause
Week 1: Train sales and CSMs; open pilot intake for 4 accounts
Weeks 2-5: Weekly negotiation cadences + engineering feasibility reviews
Week 6: Pilot decisions recorded; begin prioritized work or commercial contracts
Week 10: First delivery checkpoint for any prioritized scope
Week 14: Pilot retrospective and recommendation to scale or iterate
risks: Over-committing engineering capacity and causing roadmap slippage
Perceived unfairness from mid-market customers if top accounts receive alpha access
Legal delays on NDAs or commercial contracts increase time-to-commit
Scoring model gaming by account teams to artificially raise priority
Insufficient instrumentation to measure alpha success -> difficulty proving value
decisions: Pilot will be limited to 4 strategic accounts to reduce variability
Alpha access requires signed NDA + defined success metrics before feature work starts
Commercialized priority (paid slot) can be negotiated only if delivery window is firmed and engineering sign-off obtained
Public roadmap will not be modified for pilot requests; commitments logged in private account runways
